response.executive_summary:
This assessment examined the Deploy Notifier system, which relays deployment events from an external CI platform into an internal chat channel via a chat platform API. The approved system context models an Event Receiver and a Chat Notifier within Deploy Notifier, a CI platform and chat platform as external parties, and two key assets: deployment events and a chat bot token.

No findings were approved: no candidate weakness reached the assessment’s bar. No confirmed controls were recorded. This is not a statement that the system is secure; it reflects only that, based on the available material, no issue met the criteria for an approved finding.

The assessment instead identified six documentation gaps (five of medium significance and one of low significance) and a cluster of open, medium-priority questions. The main uncertainties concern: (1) what, if any, authentication, network controls, or rate limiting constrain access to the public Event Receiver, and how duplicate or replayed deployment events are handled; and (2) where and how the chat bot token is stored, how long it lives, how it is rotated or revoked, and whether it and the deployment events are protected in transit between the notifier and the chat platform API. Additional questions remain about rate limits, logging and possible token exposure in logs, and how the chat platform and its trust boundary are classified.

Together, these gaps mean the assessment cannot determine from documentation whether threats such as volumetric or forged deployment events, replay of prior events, or compromise and misuse of the chat bot token are effectively mitigated or whether related requirements (including req-WEBHOOK-001/002, req-SECRET-001/002, and req-DATA-001) are satisfied. Further documentation and clarification will be needed before a more definitive view of the system’s security posture can be formed.
response.system_overview:
The approved architecture models Deploy Notifier as a bridge between an external CI platform and an internal chat platform.

On the upstream side, the CI platform is both an actor and a component that sends deployment-related information as Deployment Events to the Event Receiver component. This interaction is captured as a data flow from the CI platform to the Event Receiver (df-001) and crosses a trust boundary between the external CI environment and Deploy Notifier (tb-001).

Within Deploy Notifier, the Event Receiver and Chat Notifier components form the core processing pipeline. Deployment Events are passed from the Event Receiver to the Chat Notifier (df-002). The Chat Notifier is responsible for preparing notifications about deployments, using the Deployment Events asset as input.

On the downstream side, the Chat Notifier communicates with the Chat Platform API component over a data flow from the Chat Notifier to the Chat Platform API (df-003). This flow crosses a second trust boundary between Deploy Notifier and the chat platform (tb-002). The Chat Bot Token asset is used on this integration to authenticate Deploy Notifier to the chat platform.

Engineers are recorded as an actor in the model, and the architecture captures that Deploy Notifier’s main purpose is to surface deployment information into the chat platform via the Chat Platform API, using the Deployment Events and Chat Bot Token as key assets along the described data flows and trust boundaries.
response.risk_summary:
The assessment produced no approved findings and recorded no confirmed controls. As a result, the risk summary is driven primarily by what could not be determined from the documentation, rather than by demonstrated weaknesses.

One major area of uncertainty is exposure and potential abuse of the Event Receiver. The documentation describes the Event Receiver as a public HTTPS endpoint called by the external CI platform that accepts and processes any well-formed delivery without checking a signature. At the same time, it does not establish whether any additional authentication, IP allowlisting, VPN or private ingress, or upstream rate limiting applies in front of this endpoint, nor does it document rate limits, quotas, or other bounding mechanisms for this path. It also does not describe whether deployment events carry identifiers, how duplicates are handled, or whether replayed events are detected or made harmless. These gaps prevent the assessment from determining how well the system constrains high-volume or forged deployment events or repeated submissions of old but valid-looking events, and they block a clear view of how threats associated with req-WEBHOOK-001/002 and thr-002 are managed.

A second major area concerns the custody and protection of the Chat Bot Token and the notifier–chat platform integration. While team notes state that chat posting uses a bot token held by the notifier, the available material does not document where or how this token is stored, who can access it, whether it appears in logs, how long it is valid, or how rotation and revocation are handled. Nor does it clarify whether the chat platform API is treated as an external platform under req-SECRET-001, or how that requirement applies to this token. This creates significant uncertainty about compliance with req-SECRET-001/002 and about the effort required for an attacker to obtain and exploit the token as envisioned in thr-003 and thr-005.

Related gaps affect protection of data in transit. For the data flow from the Chat Notifier to the Chat Platform API (df-003), the architecture records that encryption_in_transit is unknown, and the documentation does not specify protocol details, where TLS (if any) terminates, how the chat platform’s identity is verified, or exactly how the bot token is conveyed across the network path. Without this, the assessment cannot determine whether req-DATA-001 is satisfied for deployment notifications or whether an on-path attacker could capture or tamper with the bot token or notifications as described in thr-003 and thr-005.

Additional open questions around logging and observability (including whether logs can contain the bot token or related restricted data), the precise trust boundaries and network relationships for df-003, and the presence or absence of chat platform–level rate limits further limit confidence in any overall risk judgment. In combination, these gaps mean that the real-world likelihood and impact of several key threat scenarios, and the degree to which existing controls satisfy the cited requirements, remain materially undetermined.

limitations.text: No candidate weakness reached the assessment’s bar for an approved finding, and no confirmed controls were recorded. This is not a statement that the system is secure: the assessment’s conclusions are constrained by the available documentation, and what could not be determined is explicitly captured as documentation gaps and open questions elsewhere in the report.
